# Inverse Hyperbolic Sine

![Inverse Hyperbolic Sine function icon](../../../../assets/function-icons/functions/math/hyperbolic/07_Asinh.svg)

[Mathematics functions](../../mathematics/index.md) · [All functions](../../index.md)

Returns y such that sinh(y)=x, using the principal branch for a complex input. Input x; output arcsinh. Every real x; signed zero is preserved and asinh(±Infinity)=±Infinity. Example: Asinh(0.75) = ln(2).

## Studio authoring profile

Contract status: **partial**. The connector below describes Studio authoring; execution availability is stated separately.

<details>
<summary>Retained binding and help description</summary>

This is the source declaration, not the current measured product-execution assessment.

Returns y such that sinh(y)=x, using the principal branch for a complex input. Every real x; signed zero is preserved and asinh(±Infinity)=±Infinity. F32/F64 and finite C32/C64 inputs retain their precision; integer leaves convert to F64 before calculation and values above 2^53 may round. Arrays are processed element by element, preserving rank and dimensions; recursively numeric clusters preserve ordered fields. Typed empty arrays remain typed. String, Boolean, reference, mixed nonnumeric clusters, fixed-point, extended precision and Matrix inputs are not supported. The input x is required; the F64 unwired preview is not a numerical default. Local Highlight calculation uses frog.studio.hyperbolic.asinh. Real NaN propagates; real inputs never become complex based on their value. No angle conversion. Principal complex branches are used; non-finite complex results fail with a capability diagnostic.

Numeric scalar, array or numeric-only cluster; integer leaves produce F64 and floating-point precision is retained. Complex inverses use principal branches; non-finite complex results are unavailable. NaN propagates; real domain errors produce NaN without changing the output to complex. No angle conversion. Local Highlight calculation is available.

</details>

## Types and connection rules

F32/F64 and finite C32/C64 inputs retain their precision; integer leaves convert to F64 before calculation and values above 2^53 may round. Arrays are processed element by element, preserving rank and dimensions; recursively numeric clusters preserve ordered fields. Typed empty arrays remain typed. String, Boolean, reference, mixed nonnumeric clusters, fixed-point, extended precision and Matrix inputs are not supported. The input x is required; the F64 unwired preview is not a numerical default.

- Type resolution: `custom_resolver`; result expression: `resolve:frog.studio.hyperbolic.type-resolution@1`.
- Implicit coercion: permitted by this profile.
- Arrays: accepted; lifting policy: `element_wise_same_shape_with_scalar_lift`.
- Shape rule: `preserve_rank_dimensions_typed_empty_arrays_and_ordered_cluster_fields`.
- Scalar lifting: no.
- Broadcasting: no.

**Input count:** 1; this contract does not enable variadic inputs.

Port order: `x`.
